decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Regeneration and LGR (Leader)
purpose:
To consider the appointment of a non-executive
director to Vecteo Ltd.
content:
To consider the appointment of a non-executive
director to Vecteo Ltd.

That the appointment of Vimal
Amin as a non-executive director of the Vecteo Board, be
approved.

A recruitment campaign to fill
the vacant non-executive director post, preferably with a qualified
accountant, attracted 10 applicants. 3 were shortlisted for
interview by a panel of Sacha Jevans,
Adrienne Wright and Robert Kirton.
 
Following the interview, the
panel selected. Vimal Amin (VA) for the role. VA is a qualified
accountant with a background in school governance and community
accessibility.
 
The appointment of
Non-Executive Directors is a reserved matter for the
Shareholder.

Option 1 – To approve the
appointment of the Non-Executive Director (recommended
option).
 
Option 2 – Do nothing.
This would result in the Vecteo Board
not being able to appoint replacement Non-Executive Director to the
Board.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Regeneration and LGR (Leader)
purpose:
LTP4 covers the period 2026 to
2045 and sets out how our transport system can contribute to
Southend’s wider vision by developing and delivering a
sustainable transport network for all those who live, work in or
visit Southend.
 
It is essential that a
comprehensive consultation exercise is undertaken to ensure the
council captures the thoughts and comments of local people, local
groups and local business. Therefore, approval is sought from the
Cabinet Member for Regeneration and LGR to approve proceeding with
the public consultation from September.
content:
LTP4 covers the period 2026 to
2045 and sets out how our transport system can contribute to
Southend’s wider vision by developing and delivering a
sustainable transport network for all those who live, work in or
visit Southend.
 
It is essential that a
comprehensive consultation exercise is undertaken to ensure the
council captures the thoughts and comments of local people, local
groups and local business. Therefore, approval is sought from the
Cabinet Member for Regeneration and LGR to approve proceeding with
the public consultation from September.

That the commencement of the consultation
process for the Fourth Local Transport Plan (LTP4) from September
2026, be approved.

The reason for the decision is to enable the
Council to obtain the views of the public, statutory consultees and
other stakeholders on the draft LTP4 before it is finalised and
brought back through the appropriate decision-making process for
adoption.

It is essential that we undertake a
comprehensive consultation exercise to capture thoughts, comments,
ideas and feedback from the public and key stakeholders including
local groups and businesses. The only alternative is to not
consult, however LTPs are a statutory document and consultation is
a requirement.
 
It should be noted that following consultation
the LTP4 will be updated. Relevant and useful comments and
suggestions will be included. A full adoption process through
Cabinet will take place following this.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Finance and Transport
purpose:
Currently there are no commercial bus services
with a direct link from London Southend Airport via the east of the
City (including Temple Sutton Industrial Site and Eastern Avenue)
to the Travel Centre.

A decision is required to award the tender to the successful bus
operator for a new bus service from London Southend Airport to the
Travel Centre (via the East of the City). The new bus service is
being procured through open tender with the tender return date 12
June 2026.

The bus service is being funded by DfT LA Bus Grant revenue funding
for two years (plus 1 year subject to viability) after which the
service will be run commercially.
content:
1.            
That the award of the contract for the provision of the new bus
service, in accordance with the outcome of the procurement
exercise, be approved

 
2.            
That authority be delegated to the Executive Director for
Environment and Place, in consultation with Cabinet Member for
Finance and Transport, to finalise and authorise entering into the
contract. 

In March 2021, the Department for Transport (DfT)
published the National Bus Strategy for England titled Bus Back
Better. The Strategy set out the national policy priorities for
buses, with an overarching aim: “Our goal is to get bus use
back to what it was before the pandemic. Then we want to increase
patronage and raise buses’ mode share. We can only do these
things by ensuring that buses are an attractive alternative to the
car for far more people.”
 
Currently, there are no
commercial bus services with a direct link from LSA via the east of
the city (including Temple Farm Industrial Site, Eastern Avenue and
Wellesley Hospital) to the Travel Centre.  The proposed new bus service will be half hourly
Monday to Friday and hourly on Saturdays. The service will provide
the east of the city access to LSA and to the city centre and will
support residents within St. Laurence; Prittlewell; St.
Luke’s; Southchurch; Victoria; Kursaal; and Milton Wards. See
Appendix 1 for the proposed bus route.
 
This new bus service will also
support local businesses along the route and provide connectivity
into areas of the city that have no, or very limited, direct bus
services linking them to other parts of the city.
 
This new bus service supports the
Southend-on-Sea City Council Corporate Plan priorities by being:
safe, clean and green - providing a cleaner and more sustainable
transport option and reducing reliance on private car use; caring
with a good quality of life for all – supporting residents to
remain living independently in the community for as long as
possible; proud and prosperous – supporting local businesses;
and, led by a transformative, responsive council - addressing local
transport needs and delivering outcomes for residents through
effective partnership working.  An
improved cleaner transport system making Southend a healthier and
more accessible place to live, work and visit. 
 
This proposed new service would support access
to residents in the east of the city with LSA, the city centre and
seafront area.  Providing and supporting
people in living, ageing and caring well and remain living
independently in the community for as long as possible.  The new bus service also supports thriving
businesses, a strong local economy, a healthier, more productive
labour market and people proud to live and work in
Southend-on-Sea.
 
This new bus service supports
government’s ambitions to get people using public transport
and will support access for residents and businesses in St.
Laurence; Prittlewell; St. Luke’s; Southchurch; Victoria;
Kursaal and Milton Wards.
 
The new bus service was tendered for a
two-year period with the potential to receive a further one-year of
support, subject to performance and grant funding.  The tenders were evaluated on the basis of 70%
price and 30% quality. The three bids that were received are from
existing bus operators who currently operate services within the
city. All three bids were compliant and met the requirements of the
procurement process. 
 
The majority of the bus route benefits from
existing infrastructure. However, six new bus stops are proposed in
both directions (northbound & southbound) along the new
route.  Also, existing bus stop
infrastructure along the route will be upgraded to improve
accessibility. DfT Local Area Bus Grant (LABG) capital funding is
available and will fund the new and upgraded infrastructure
works.

The alternative option is not to provide a new
bus service and residents will access the Airport, Wellesley
Hospital, city centre and leisure facilities as they currently do
either by driving, hiring a taxi, or not making the journey at all.
Employees working within the industrial areas served by the
proposed route would also continue to rely largely on car travel,
limiting transport choices and disadvantaging those who do not have
access to a private vehicle.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Technology, Learning and Customer Services
purpose:
Following a reduction in birth rate and fall
in the number of pupils within the local area the Local Authority
and School have reviewed the admission number at Leigh North Street
Primary School. The application is to reduce the admission number
at the school from 90 to 60, to support financial planning and
education outcomes at the school.
content:
The Cabinet Member
for Technology, Learning and Customer Care agrees to:
 

1.    
Approve the principle of a submission to the OSA to authorise
the variation of the determined admission arrangements for the
School by reducing the reception PAN
from 90 places to 60 with effect from September 2027; and

 

2.    
Delegate authority to the Executive Director for Children and
Public Health, in consultation with the Director of Education,
Inclusion and Early Years, to:

 
a) consult with the
School;
b) finalise and submit
the application and supporting evidence and to respond to any
further information requested by the OSA; and
     c) notify the prescribed bodies
upon confirmation of any variation.

Birth rates have been falling across
Southend-on-Sea since 2015, with the effect becoming increasingly
evident in reception intakes from the early 2020s. Live births fell
from 2,213 in 2015/16 to 1,581 in 2021/22, with lower cohorts
forecast to continue through the period relevant to admissions in
2027, 2028 and 2029.

School capacity is based upon thresholds of 30
children.  For each threshold that is
reached, there are specific requirements around provision of
teachers and support.  Each threshold is
referred to as a ‘form of entry’.  Therefore, reducing 90 places to 60, is a
reduction from 3 forms of entry, to 2 forms of entry.

Without further intervention, surplus reception capacity across the
city is forecast to reach approximately 12% by 2029/30. Since 2020,
the Council has worked with school leaders to remove a net 11 forms
of entry of surplus primary capacity where evidence has
demonstrated this to be appropriate. These changes have enabled the
Council to respond to falling demand while maintaining sufficient
school places and parental choice across the City. Current
modelling indicates that a further reduction of approximately 11
forms of entry across the City may be required over the next four
years to restore surplus capacity to a sustainable range of
5–8%.
 
The School is within the Leigh Planning Area.
There are currently 570 Reception places across seven schools in
the area. Forecast demand is 468 places for 2027, 540 for 2028 and
442 for 2029, producing forecast surplus capacity of approximately
25%, 14% and 29% respectively if no mitigating action is taken.
 
The September 2026 allocation position
indicates approximately 133 vacant Reception places across the
Leigh Planning Area, equivalent to a surplus of around 23%. We are
seeing a continual reduction in the number of parents requesting
the School as its first preference that shows a lower demand for
the School. The figures support this reduction in demand:
 

a.    
For September 2026, it received 60 first preferences, which is
lower than the available spaces and

b.    
Its total preferences reduced form 222 in 2024 to 176 in 2026.
 
The planning area is densely developed, has
limited scope for substantial new housing and currently has no
significant housing development expected to generate additional
short-term demand. Although pupil forecasts will continue to be
reviewed and longer-term Local Plan development may increase
demand, the current evidence supports action to reduce excess
capacity now. Forecasts are reviewed annually and, should demand
increase materially in future years, admission arrangements can be
reconsidered through the statutory admissions process.
 
A reduction from 90 to 60 places would remove
1 form of entry and align the school’s published capacity
more closely with forecast demand. Sufficient places would remain
available within the planning area to meet forecast demand and
support parental preference.
 
The admission arrangements for September 2027
have already been determined. Consequently, the Council cannot
amend the PAN unilaterally and must request a variation from the
OSA. The OSA will consider the evidence, the Council’s
sufficiency duty (providing a place for every child plus a surplus
of 3-7%) and the capacity of local schools to meet parental
preference before making its decision.
 

Do not submit a variation request. This would
retain a PAN of 90 for September 2027 despite evidence of sustained
surplus capacity and declining demand. This option is not
recommended because it would limit the Council’s ability to
manage the primary estate sustainably and could increase financial
and organisational pressures on the school and neighbouring
provision.
 
Seek a different level or timing of reduction.
A reduction of one form of entry from September 2027 is considered
proportionate to the evidence currently available. Forecasts will
continue to be reviewed and any further changes would be considered
separately through the appropriate statutory admissions
process.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Finance and Transport
purpose:
Tender outcome for Intelligent Transport
Systems including traffic signals, variable message signs and car
park signs and award of contract to the successful bidder
content:
That the award of the contract
for Intelligent Transport Systems including traffic signals,
variable message signs and car park signs to YUNEX Limited
commencing on 1st November 2026 for a period of 4 years with an
option to extend the contract by a further 4 years, be
approved.

The current contract for
Intelligent Transport Systems including traffic signals, variable
message signs and car park signs concludes on 31st
October 2026.
 
A procurement
process was undertaken to establish a new contract from
1st November 2026.  The
process followed the requirements of the Procurement Act
2023.  The competitive flexible
procedure was used.  An advert was
placed for an above threshold contract on the national Find a
Tender Service portal.  All potential
bidders were given an opportunity for a meeting with the Council to
clarify any of the requirements of the tender.  Any bidder was then free to submit a tender for
the Council to evaluate i.e. there was no restriction or
shortlisting of bidders. 
 
Two bidders
submitted tenders to  be considered for
the new contract.
 
The tender
process was undertaken under the Procurement Act 2023
requirements.
 
Tender submissions were
received by 23rd July 2026, and a full evaluation
process was undertaken. The outcome is based on a 60/40 split
between quality and commercial respectively. The commercial
submissions are against the required Schedule of Rates to be used
within the contract. The Quality submissions were reviewed under
the following key headings for delivering the requirements of the
Contract:
1. Mobilisation
2. Maintenance service –
traffic signals
3. Maintenance service –
all other equipment
4. Annual
inspections
5. Service to supply and
install new equipment
6. Social Value – social
value
7. Social Value – carbon
management
 
Tenders were evaluated by 3
evaluators and then scores were moderated to agree final
scores. 
 
Yunex Limited submitted the most
advantageous tender i.e. Yunex Limited
scored the highest marks against the evaluation
criteria.
 
Assessment summaries have been
issued to the successful and unsuccessful bidders advising them of
the outcome of the evaluation on 4th August
2026.  As is required by the Procurement
Act 2023, the Council then published a UK6 Contract Award Notice on
the national portal (the Find a tender Service) on 4th
August 2026.    It is not
awarding the contract as that can only take place once this report
has been authorised by the relevant Cabinet Member.   The UK6 Contract Award Notice is necessary
to commence a mandatory standstill period during which unsuccessful
bidders can challenge the award.  If the
Cabinet Member approves this report, the Council will then be able
to move to awarding the contract (i.e. sign the contract or enter
into the contract) and will then have to publish a further notice
– a UK7 Contract Details Notice.
 

The only other option at this
stage is to not award and restart the tender process. That would
require a further extension to the current contract and the
potential for legal challenge as we have exceeded the value of the
original contract. In addition, this would attract further staff
and legal support costs

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Technology, Learning and Customer Services
purpose:
To award a 3-year contract (with the option to
extend for a further 12 months) with a supplier to complete the
current refresh cycle for the procurement of laptops.
content:
That the award of a contract,
following a compliant tender process, for the supply of end user
devices as part of the Council’s Device Refresh Programme, be
awarded to the successful suppliers as set out in confidential
Appendix A to this decision record for a period of 3 years with an
optional extension of 12 months. 
 
That the Executive Director for
Strategy and Change, in consultation with the S151 Officer, and
Monitoring Officer be delegated authority to agree all necessary
contractual documentation associated with the award.
 

Background and
Drivers
 
The Council previously approved
a rolling refresh programme for end user devices, based on a
lifecycle of approximately 3–4 years. This approach ensures
continued access to secure and supported hardware.
 
Changes to national procurement
arrangements mean that aggregated procurements are no longer
available. As a result, the Council has undertaken its own
compliant procurement process via a Public Sector
Framework.
 
A new contract is required to
maintain continuity of supply and support the ongoing refresh of
laptops, desktops, and associated equipment.
 
Procurement Process and Policy
Outcomes
 
A compliant further competition
was undertaken through an appropriate CCS framework, in accordance
with the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules and applicable
procurement legislation.
 
The procurement process
included the issue of a specification, evaluation of bids against
published quality and price criteria, moderation of scores,
confirmation of affordability, and a final e-auction stage. The
e-auction stage enabled the Council to ensure best value for the
price submission for each bidder. The outcome of the procurement
process and e-auction identified the most economically advantageous
tender.
 
The contract award supports the
Council’s Corporate Plan priorities by ensuring continuity,
resilience, and value for money in the provision of a critical
corporate service. 
 
Contract Management
 
The contract will be managed by
the Technology service in accordance with the Council’s
contract management guidelines.
 
Performance will be monitored
against agreed key performance indicators (KPIs) and service level
agreements (SLAs), with regular supplier review meetings and
defined escalation routes.
 
Financial performance will be
monitored through existing budget management processes aligned to
the Medium-Term Financial Strategy (MTFS).
 
The contract will be subject to
regular operational review, including monitoring of delivery
against agreed milestones, performance.

Option 1 – Not
recommended. Lease devices from a supplier/manufacturer. This
approach would see the council enter into a lease agreement with a
supplier for a fixed period. The benefits of this approach are a
much lower upfront cost with monthly, quarterly, or annual
payments. Additional supplier support could be provided throughout
the lease (maintenance, break fix, replacement etc). This approach
changes the method of funding from Capital to Revenue. The approach
also creates restrictions on how the equipment is used and at the
end of the lease equipment needs to be returned to the
Lessor
 
Option 2 –
Recommended. Procure devices via a tender
process and replace on a rolling basis.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Technology, Learning and Customer Services
purpose:
Cabinet Member
approval is sought for the award of a contract for the replacement
of the Council’s telephony and contact centre platforms.
content:
Cabinet Member
approval is sought for the award of a contract for the replacement
of the Council’s telephony and contact centre platforms.

1. That the award of the contract for the
replacement telephony and contact centre platform to the
second-ranked bidder from the completed procurement process, for an
initial term of 3 years from the contract commencement date, with
the option to extend for up to a further 2 years, be approved.
 
2. That authority be delegated to the
Executive Director for Strategy and Change, in consultation with
the Section 151 Officer and Monitoring Officer, to finalise and
agree the contractual documentation required to complete the award,
provided that it remains consistent with
the procurement outcome, approved budget and terms of this
decision.
 
3. That authority be delegate to the Executive
Director for Strategy and Change, in consultation with the Cabinet
Member for Technology, Learning and Customer Services, to exercise
the contractual extension options of up to two further years,
subject to satisfactory supplier performance, continued service
requirement, affordability and compliance with the terms of the
contract.

The proposed award to the
second-ranked bidder provides a compliant route to implementing the
replacement solution, maintaining service continuity and avoiding
the delay and additional resource requirements associated with
restarting the procurement.
 

1. Proceed with Vodafone: Not
recommended. Vodafone was originally identified as the preferred
bidder, but the Counncil has been
unable to agree contractual terms that are consistent with the
tendered and evaluated position. Accepting material post-tender
changes would create procurement and legal risk and would reduce
confidence in delivery.
 
2. Restart the procurement: Not
recommended. A new procurement would introduce significant delay,
increase officer and supplier effort, defer delivery benefits and
increase the risk of continued dependence on ageing telephony
infrastructure during a period of organisational change.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Planning, Property and Governance
purpose:
To endorse the
updated Essex Coast Recreational disturbance Avoidance and
Mitigation Strategy (RAMS). The strategy sets out the mitigation
requirements relating to impacts from increased recreation (linked
to the in-combination effects of housing growth and tourist
development across the county) on important nature conservation
sites on the Essex coast.

It updates and replaces the previously agreed strategy (approved in
2020) and relates to 12 relevant Local Planning Authorities (LPAs)
that comprise the greater part of the Essex Coast Recreational
disturbance Avoidance and Mitigation Strategy (RAMS)
Partnership.

The RAMS ensures
these authorities are adequately protecting the relevant wildlife
sites from the impacts of recreation), while mitigating the impacts
of new housing in a timely manner. This strategic mitigation is
required to comply with the Conservation of Habitats and Species
Regulations 2017, as amended, (commonly referred to as the
‘Habitats Regulations’).
content:
To endorse the
updated Essex Coast Recreational disturbance Avoidance and
Mitigation Strategy (RAMS). The strategy sets out the mitigation
requirements relating to impacts from increased recreation (linked
to the in-combination effects of housing growth and tourist
development across the county) on important nature conservation
sites on the Essex coast.

It updates and replaces the previously agreed strategy (approved in
2020) and relates to 12 relevant Local Planning Authorities (LPAs)
that comprise the greater part of the Essex Coast Recreational
disturbance Avoidance and Mitigation Strategy (RAMS)
Partnership.

The RAMS ensures
these authorities are adequately protecting the relevant wildlife
sites from the impacts of recreation), while mitigating the impacts
of new housing in a timely manner. This strategic mitigation is
required to comply with the Conservation of Habitats and Species
Regulations 2017, as amended, (commonly referred to as the
‘Habitats Regulations’).

1. That the revised and updated
Essex Coast Recreational disturbance Avoidance and Mitigation
Strategy (Essex Coast RAMS), as set out in APPENDIX 1 to this
report, superseding the original Essex Coast RAMS (2018-2038)
documen, be approvedt;
 
2. That the Essex Coast RAMS
Technical Advice Note (TAN) as set out in APPENDIX 2 of this
report, which will be used as a material consideration in relevant
planning decisions, ensuring that the transition from SPD to TAN
does not create a policy gap, supporting consistent implementation
of the Essex Coast RAMS strategy across the Essex Coast RAMS
partnership area, enabling ongoing compliance with the Habitats
Regulations and providing certainty that decision-making remains
robust and defensible, be approved;
 
3. That the Executive Director
for Environment and Place be authorised to make minor amendments to
the above TAN as deemed necessary before publication;
 
4. That the Essex Coast RAMS
Supplementary Planning Document (SPD) (2020) be revoked as the
content of the document is no longer fully aligned with the 2026
revised Essex Coast RAMS Strategy, evidence base and
tariff.  The revocation statement as
shown in APPENDIX 5 of this report, must be published on the
Council’s website and all copies of the SPD
removed.

Southend-on-Sea City Council is
one of twelve partner local authorities who have been working
together, in consultation with Natural England, on the review and
update to the Essex Coast Recreational disturbance Avoidance and
Mitigation Strategy (Essex Coast RAMS 2018-2038).  A review of the strategy was undertaken in 2025-6
to ensure it remains fit for purpose, evidence-led and legally
robust.
 
The Essex Coast
RAMS aims to prevent bird and habitat disturbance from recreational
activities through a package of strategic access management
measures and monitoring designed to influence how people access and
use the coast, encouraging visitors to enjoy their visits in a
responsible manner.  The mitigation
package includes coastal rangers, information signs and
interpretation, advice for dog walkers and other users of the
coastline, surveys and monitoring. The measures are funded through
pooled developer contributions, allowing mitigation to be
strategically planned, rather than ad hoc on a site-by-site
basis.
 
The Essex Coast
RAMS strategic mitigation enables the Council, in its role as
Competent Authority, to meet its statutory duties under section 63
(1) of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017(as
amended).  The revised strategy provides
long?term, in?perpetuity mitigation for recreational impacts on
internationally designated coastal sites while enabling planned
development to proceed. It is an approach that has been endorsed by
Natural England (see Natural England letter set out at APPENDIX 3
to this report).
 
Essex Coast RAMS
has been used successfully in the determination of planning
applications since 2020. A Supplementary Planning Document (SPD)
was also produced and adopted to summarise the Essex Coast RAMS
into a concise guide for developers, demonstrating why mitigation
is needed.  New SPDs generally cannot be produced in the same way as before
because of legislative changes (Levelling up and Regeneration Act
2023), so a TAN has been produced jointly by the 12 local
authorities in the partnership to provide consistent advice for
developers on how the Essex Coast RAMS tariff will work in
practice.
 
On approval of the TAN the
Essex Coast RAMS 2018-2038 will be formally revoked, as it is no
longer aligned with the 2026 revised Essex Coast RAMS Strategy,
evidence base and tariff. As required under Regulation 15 of the
Town and Country Planning (Local Planning) (England) Regulations
2012 (as amended), following the revocation of the SPD, all
physical and digital copies of the document will no longer be
available, effective from 1st August 2026.

Do not endorse the updated
Essex Coast RAMS Strategy and increased Essex Coast RAMS tariff and
maintain the RAMS tariff at the current rate.
 
Continuation of the tariff at
the current rate would not adequately reflect up to date evidence
including new visitor survey data and local plan housing
requirements. Not having an adequate mitigation scheme in place
could cause uncertainty for developers, and may require bespoke
mitigation schemes, as Natural England and other parties could
argue that the level of mitigation of in-combination impacts is not
sufficient to prevent harm to designated habitats sites, and object
to individual planning applications on that basis. 
 
A reduced tariff which does not
cover the full costs of mitigation could also place undue financial
burdens on the Council as Competent Authority, as we would need to
cover the shortfall under the Partnership Agreement (clause
6.2.3.9), as set out in APPENDIX
6.
 
The tariff approach has been
successfully implemented to date and supported at appeal. Overall,
a strategic mitigation scheme that factors in the impacts of
anticipated growth across the Essex Coast RAMS area, as is in place
at many other designated habitats sites in England, is the
preferred option to individual assessments. It is endorsed by
Natural England, and is a solution that has been in place, working
well in Southend since 2020.
 
There is likely to be
associated legal risks with maintaining a dated mitigation package
that does not adequately reflect the up-to-date
evidence.  This could result in
additional costs to the Council in the longer term.
 
No other options have been
identified.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Planning, Property and Governance has decided to endorse the updated Essex Coast Recreational disturbance Avoidance and Mitigation Strategy to protect important nature conservation sites from the impacts of increased recreation.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Health and Social Care Act 2012 requires
Directors of Public Health to prepare an annual report on the
health of the local population.
content:
The Cabinet considered a report of the
Executive Director of Children and Public Health which presented
the Annual Public Health report 2025-26.
 
Reasons for Decision(s)
 
The Council has a statutory duty to protect
the health of the local population. The 2025-26 Annual Public
Health Report highlights some of the key issues and proposed
actions to address them for the people in Southend city.
 
Resolved:
 
That the Annual Public Health Report 2025-26,
as set out at Appendix 1 to the submitted report, be noted.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to note the Annual Public Health Report 2025-26 to address key health issues in Southend city.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
To agree the next phases of Council’s
retrofit programme and resettlement acquisitions
programme
content:
The Cabinet considered a report of the
Executive Director of Environment and Place which outlined the
funding parameters and additional co-funding required to match two
funding opportunities to support the outcomes of the Housing
Pressures Action Plan; the Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund Wave 3
and the Local Authority Housing Fund (LAHF) Round 4.
 
Reasons for Decision(s)
 
Retrofitting properties reduces energy bills
for residents. The upgrades delivered through this funding are
likely to deliver annual fuel savings to residents of around
£321 on average (drawn from modelling work on Parity),
although actual savings could be higher depending on use and tariff
choice. This will lead to an average combined yearly saving of
£29,853.
 
Retrofitting 93 council homes will assist the
Council in meeting its longer-term energy efficiency obligations
including adherence with the proposed Minimum Energy Efficiency
Standards (MEES) which requires all social homes to meet EPC C
standard by 2030.
 
Carbon reduction: Improving a property to EPC
C for a local authority will deliver on average a 0.8t CO2 saving
per year. This is approximately a third of the annual average
emissions of 2.4t CO2 per household. This means that across this
project there will be an average 74.4t CO2 saving per year.
 
Acquiring new council homes including
temporary accommodation is a key outcome of the Housing Pressures
Action Plan. Attracting grant from Government will help to ensure
that the previously agreed budgets can be stretched further and
enable the Council to purchase more homes than originally planned,
providing the potential to bring more families out of expensive
nightly lets and into settled, better value accommodation with
better outcomes for them.
 
Resolved:
 
That it be agreed that Cabinet:
 
1.         Notes
the ongoing application for up to £930,000 of additional
grant funding through the Warm Homes: Social Housing Fund Wave
3.
 
2.         Agrees
to use up to £550k from the Housing Revenue Account (HRA)
Capital Reserves for 2026/27 for match funding and contingency
costs in order bring the project forward and retrofit 93 council
homes.
 
3.        
Delegates authority to the Executive Director for Environment and
Place to sign, or authorise completion of contracts for delivery of
the 2026/27 additional grant funded activity.
 
4.         Agrees
to use £951k from the existing Housing Pressures Action Plan
budgets from 26/27 – 29/30 for match funding Local Authority

content:
To approve the
award of a four-year contract for the maintenance, inspection and
repair of lifting equipment used within the Occupational Therapy
and Community Equipment Service.

The decision
seeks approval to award a contract with a total value of
£579,024 over four years for the inspection, maintenance and
repair of lifting equipment provided to disabled children and
adults within Southend-on-Sea.

The contract is funded through the Disabled Facilities Grant (DFG)
and associated adaptations budgets and is expected to commence in
July 2026.

The
Cabinet Member for Social Care & Healthier Communities agrees
to: 
 
(1)
Approve the award of a four-year contract for the maintenance,
inspection and repair of lifting equipment as detailed within the
accompanying Part 2 exempt Tender Acceptance Report.
 
(2)
Authorise the Executive Director for Adults and Communities to
agree all necessary contractual documentation associated with the
award.
 

The
Council has a continuing requirement for a compliant maintenance,
inspection and repair service for lifting equipment provided to
disabled children and adults. Awarding the contract will ensure
continuity of service provision from 10 July 2026 and enable the
Council to continue meeting its statutory responsibilities relating
to the maintenance and safety of lifting equipment.
 
Failure to award the contract would expose the Council to the
risk of being unable to meet its statutory duties in respect of the
provision and maintenance of equipment for disabled residents under
the Care Act 2014, Children Act 1989 and the Chronically Sick and
Disabled Persons Act 1970.
 

The
option of extending the existing contractual arrangements was
considered but was not available within the terms of the current
contract.
 
The
option of delivering the service in-house was considered but
discounted due to the specialist nature of the service, the
requirement for appropriately qualified engineers and inspectors,
and the infrastructure required to deliver a compliant maintenance
and inspection service.
 
The
option of not awarding a contract was considered and rejected as
this would leave the Council unable to meet its statutory
responsibilities for the inspection, maintenance and repair of
lifting equipment provided to disabled children and adults and
would create significant operational, safety and compliance
risks.
 
The
recommended option is to award the contract following completion of
a compliant procurement process as detailed within the accompanying
Part 2 exempt Tender Acceptance Report.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities has decided to award a four-year contract for the maintenance, inspection, and repair of lifting equipment in Southend-on-Sea.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities
purpose:
To seek approval for a special urgency
decision to directly award contracts to current suppliers
of the existing Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) contract for
Section 12 (s12) Doctors to undertake assessments under the
Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) for a further 12 months. The current contract
expires at the end of June 2026 and there is insufficient time
to complete a full procurement process. The proposed direct
award will ensure continuity of statutory services while
further work is undertaken to determine future
commissioning arrangements, particularly considering the
recent AGNI Supreme Court judgment and ongoing
legislative and practice uncertainty. AGNI changed the
legal test for deprivation of liberty and introduces
uncertainty in the interpretation of liberty
and consent; a shorter contract is considered prudent
pending greater legal and operational clarity.
content:
To seek approval for a special urgency
decision to directly award contracts to current suppliers
of the existing Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) contract for
Section 12 (s12) Doctors to undertake assessments under the
Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) for a further 12 months. The current contract
expires at the end of June 2026 and there is insufficient time
to complete a full procurement process. The proposed direct
award will ensure continuity of statutory services while
further work is undertaken to determine future
commissioning arrangements, particularly considering the
recent AGNI Supreme Court judgment and ongoing
legislative and practice uncertainty. AGNI changed the
legal test for deprivation of liberty and introduces
uncertainty in the interpretation of liberty
and consent; a shorter contract is considered prudent
pending greater legal and operational clarity. 
 

The Cabinet Member
for Social Care and Healthier Communities agrees to:-
                       
Approve, under
special urgency provisions, the direct award of the DPS contract
for s12 Doctors for a period of 12 months from 1 July 2026 to 30
June 2027, with a value of £290,300.
 

The Council commissions s12 Doctors via a DPS
to undertake statutory   mental
health assessments under DoLS. The
original contract was established in 2018 for a period of four
years, with an option to extend for a further 4 years. This
extension has now been fully utilised and expires on
30th June 2026 however as this is a PSR procurement we
have the option to directly award a contract to the current
providers, and then we are able to run a new process to start a new
DPS/framework and try and attract new providers for the next
contract.
 
A direct award is required to maintain
continuity of the statutory DoLS
assessment services and ensure compliance with legal duties.
Without the award of this contract, there is significant risk of
service disruption, increased delays in assessments, and potential
legal challenge.
 
The recent AGNI Supreme Court Judgement
introduces uncertainty into future demand and operating models,
making a short-term extension the most proportionate approach while
longer-term implications are assessed.
 

The undertaking of an immediate full
procurement process was considered; however, this is not now
feasible within the required timescales without risking service
interruption.
 
A range of issues were encountered during the
procurement process. Initially    an issue was identified that this
procurement was not included on the forward plan. Secondly the
intention was to proceed with a 2-year contract and the projected
spend was noted as being within Exec Director approval levels
rather than Cabinet approval, however it was identified that whilst
the spend was within limits, the recorded budget was not, which
meant that this approach was not feasible. As the deadline
approached a Procedural/ Tender Exception option was pursued
however was latterly identified as beyond the total spend limit and
was therefore not a feasible option. Due to the timescale a special
urgency approach is being pursued.
 
Ceasing or reducing the service is not an
option, as this would place the Council in breach of its statutory
duties under DoLS legislation.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities has decided to approve the direct award of contracts to current suppliers for Section 12 Doctors to undertake assessments under the Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) for a further 12 months.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Council currently has a contract in place
for the provision at a corporate level for all hybrid and
transactional mail. The current contract expires on 31st August
2026 but has an option to extend for a further 24 months. To enable
the continuation of these services for all Southend-on-Sea City
Council Departments, this report is seeking approval to trigger
this extension to the contract until 31st August 2028.
content:
The Cabinet considered a report of the
Executive Director (Finance and Resources) which sought approval to
extend the existing transactional print and hybrid mail contract
for a period of 24 months expiring on 31 August 2028.
 
Reasons for decision(s):
 
There is still a requirement to have printing
and mailing services available to the City Council.
 
To extend the current contract under the
original terms and conditions, noting that further work will be
undertaken, provides assurance over service continuity and value
for money. The Council have experienced no issues with the
operation of the current contract provider, and this extension will
provide the opportunity to explore further ways of reducing the
volumes and costs of this service over the next 2 years. This
option also avoids the costs associated with a new procurement
exercise. Internal efforts will continue to ensure the most
cost-effective solution is adopted for all services across the City
Council.
 
As we prepare for the outcome of Local
Government Reorganisation a contract extension for these services
is pragmatic, reasonable and provides good value for money.
 
Consideration of this item did not move into
exempt session, although it was noted that the report contained an
exempt appendix under paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Schedule 12A of the
Local Government Act 1972, as it included information relating to
the financial or business affairs of the authority holding that
information.
 
Resolved:-
 
That Cabinet approve the extension of the
Council’s existing Hybrid and Transactional Mail with Ricoh
Print Services for a period of 24 months expiring on 31 August
2028.

content:
The Transport
Strategy Team are progressing an update of the Council’s
Multi-Modal Transport Model.

The model needs to be updated, with accurate traffic-flow data and
growth scenarios, to enable the Council to understand the impact of
future growth, development proposals and transport schemes
delivered in Southend, the city and beyond.

The required funding allocation has been identified and submitted
to January Cabinet and Full Council.

Members are asked to note and approve the requirement for officers
to undertake a tender process and award the modelling contract
through delegated authority to Executive and Director level.
 

1)
That the procurement of a contract for a Multi-Modal Transport
Model (MMTM) be approved and;
 
2)
Authority be delegated to the Executive Director for Environment
and Place to award the Multi-Modal Transport Model (MMTM) contract
in accordance with the outcome of the procurement
exercise.
 

The existing MMTM needs to be
updated in accordance with the Department for Transport’s
(DfT) guidance. The current model is based on 2018 data and
therefore the model needs to be updated with current traffic data
and growth scenarios.
 
This will ensure compliance
with the DfT’s Transport Appraisal Guidance (TAG) to enable
the Council to understand the impact of future growth, development
proposals and major transport schemes and how they can be delivered
in Southend and beyond to align with the Council’s emerging
Fourth Local Transport Plan (LTP4) and our strategic direction for
transport. Many large-scale development applications are being
submitted, and the model is used to assess the potential impact
developments have on the highway network. The model is also used to
secure DfT funding for major transport schemes.
 

To not procure and appoint a
transport modelling consultancy and undertake the work internally.
The expertise required to update and maintain a transport model is
not currently available in the Council and does not give value for
money.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Regeneration and LGR has decided to update the Council's Multi-Modal Transport Model to understand the impact of future growth and development proposals.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities
purpose:
To approve the variation of the Southend
Treatment and Recovery Service Contract to provide additional grant
funding in 2026-27 to support the delivery of the National Drug
Strategy.
content:
To approve the variation of the Southend
Treatment and Recovery Service Contract to provide additional grant
funding in 2026-27 to support the delivery of the National Drug
Strategy.

1. That the contract variation to the contract with Forward
Trust to increase the total annual funding for the Southend
Treatment and Recovery Service (STARS) contract by £1,096,022
in 2026/27, be approved.
 
2, That authority be delegated to the Executive Director
(Adults and Communities) to undertake all necessary actions
including finalising the terms of the contract and entering into
the agreement.

1. The contract for the
Southend Treatment and Recovery Service was awarded to Forward
Trust on 1st April 2022, expiring on 31st March 2027,
with the option to extend until 31st March 2032. Since
then, the contract has been varied each year to specify additional
funds that will be made available to the treatment service and to
include additional requirements associated with this supplementary
grant funding.
 
2.
The contract for the Southend Treatment and Recovery Service was
awarded to Forward Trust on 1st April 2022, expiring on
31st March 2027, with the option to extend until 31st
March 2032. Since then, the contract has been varied each year to
specify additional funds that will be made available to the
treatment service and to include additional requirements associated
with this supplementary grant funding.
 

1. Do nothing - If the Council does not approve
this contract variation, there will be significant challenges
in meeting the requirements of the grant funding and ambitions
agreed with OHID around increasing treatment capacity and quality.
There would also be significant risks to current service delivery,
as the additional roles funded over the past 4 years will not be
able to be delivered without the provision of this additional grant
funding, risking a destablilisation of the service. By
not utilizing this additional grant funding,
the Council would miss an opportunity to uphold its
statutory public health duty to
improve population health and meet the ambitions of
various national, regional and local
strategies. 
 
2. Conduct a procurement exercise to enable other providers
to bid for the funding Forward Trust currently provides a
comprehensive and integrated treatment and recovery service for
people requiring support with their drug and/ or alcohol use. This
includes an integrated team of specialist staff who can deliver a
range of interventions and treatment options such as psychosocial,
pharmacological and psychological approaches, as well as clinical
management and recovery support through a range of mutual aid
interventions. Procuring a separate organization to deliver the
proposed roles is not recommended, as the Forward Trust already has
a well-established team who work together to ensure efficient and
effective use of resources and skills, ensuring the full range of
interventions can be made available to the client as part of their
treatment plan. It would also come with additional cost
implications to ensure a robust management structure and clinical
governance/ supervision is in place for the staff occupying the
proposed roles.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities has decided to approve additional grant funding for the Southend Treatment and Recovery Service Contract to support the delivery of the National Drug Strategy.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Climate, Environment, and Waste
purpose:
Approval of the Essex Air Quality Strategy
2025 and action plan and supporting information document.
content:
That the Essex Air Quality strategy, the
action plan and the supporting information document be
approved, adopted and formally published.

As set out in the decision
report.

Option 1 (recommended): Agree
to adopt and formally publish the Essex Air Quality strategy, and
the action plan, as appended to this report. This will be published
on the EssexAir website,  (www.essexair.org.uk) on behalf of the Essex Air Quality
Consortium, and a link to the strategy will be provided on
Southend-on-Sea City Council’s website. 
 
Option 2 (not recommended):
Progress with finalising a joint Air Quality Strategy but do not
publish or work further with partner organisations on this
matter. This risks completing a strategy that does not
have full buy in from partner organisations
and doesn’t benefit from external
visibility.  
 
Option 3 (not recommended): Do
not progress any further work on a joint Air Quality Strategy. This
would result in considerable abortive work for all the local
authorities and partners involved in the development of the
strategy to date. Furthermore, without a strategy, the Essex
Air Quality Consortium is less likely to be able
to benefit from public and private funding opportunities
for improving air quality.   
 
Option 4 (not recommended): Do
not approve and adopt the Air Quality
Strategy. When the Council revoke their Air Quality
Management Area’s we will need to produce an Air
Quality Strategy as required by the Local Air Quality
Management (LAQM) Regime and in line with
Defra’s requirements. This would result in formal
consultation and resource implications.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Climate, Environment, and Waste has decided to approve and adopt the Essex Air Quality strategy and action plan.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities
purpose:
To enable an effective and safe transition
over to South Essex Homes (SEH), the commissioning team are
requesting that the start of the contractual arrangements with SEH
is deferred until 1st July 2026, and are requesting a further
extension of the SMDS contract for 3-months until 30th June
2026.
content:
1. A review of the transition planning process
with the SMDS / IHS provider has highlighted some significant risks
in terms of the timescales relating to staff notice, consultation
requirements and tenancy agreements for the current tenants.
Current staff require at a minimum 3-months’ notice, and
residents 2 months.
 
2. In addition, although the specification is
complete, the process to move the service in-house involves a level
of work with SEH to establish how they will deliver against the
specification and to outline this in the partnership agreement held
between the Council and SEH. It is pertinent that this is done in
collaboration with the incumbent providers to ensure a robust
transition of the services, which in turn has meant that the
original timeframes predicted for a tender process are not
sufficient to deliver the mobilisation effectively in transferring
the service over to SEH.

1. Do nothing/ Transition the
service over before 1st April 2026 this option is not
recommended. Transitioning the service over before negotiations are
complete poses a great risk to staff stability and retention, as
well as existing tenants. The residents supported by the incumbent
provider have a high level of need, and multiple vulnerabilities,
so ensuring the service transition is managed robustly, and in
collaboration with the incumbent provider, is key.
 
2. Implement the full 12 month
extension of the SMDS contract - this option is not recommended.
Extensive work has been undertaken to review the existing model and
agree upon the preferred commissioning option. Extending for
another year would just further delay the transition and would mean
the delivery of this contract would not be in alignment with the
wider transition of the transitional supported housing contract
over to SEH.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities has decided to not transition the supported housing service before 1st April 2026, citing risks to staff stability and retention, as well as the well-being of vulnerable residents.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Climate, Environment, and Waste
purpose:
Approval of a policy to ensure that the
Council has a clear and consistent approach to how it will deal
with covenants over park land which provides flexibility and
pragmatism while also recognising the importance of covenants
affecting its land.
content:
That the adoption of the
following policy position in relation to restrictive covenants in
parks be approved:
 
1. Covenants affecting
designated parks and open spaces are already subject to a high
degree of protection through title registration and the need to
advertise any proposed disposal pursuant to Local Government Act
1972 (s.123);
 
2. In addition to these
protections, and subject to 3 below, the Council will operate a
general presumption in favour of upholding covenants affecting its
park land and ensure that no development occurs in parks without
proper consideration. Officers must check the registered title for
covenants and engage with relevant stakeholders where covenants
exist;
 
3. While the Council is
committed to engaging and consulting, this does not imply
indefinite adherence to covenants or publicly consulting where for
example, modification or insurance may be reasonable and pragmatic
options; and
 
4. The engagement or
consultation process will be flexible on a case by case basis,
determined by the Executive Director for Environment and Place in
consultation with the Cabinet Member with responsibility for Parks
and with input from legal services as appropriate to ensure that
any covenants are duly considered whilst still ensuring
infrastructure can be installed, or development can proceed where
it is deemed the best option.
 
5. That the Executive Director
for Environment and Place shall be authorised to implement this
policy.

To ensure that the Council has
a clear and consistent approach to how it will deal with
covenants over park land which
provides flexibility and pragmatism while also recognising the
importance of covenants affecting its land.

The Council could continue
without a clear policy on covenants, relying on the basis that they
contained in legal documents and registered against the title of
land.  Restrictive covenants would be
considered and dealt with as required by officers, particularly in
the Asset Management and Legal teams. 
However, this option would not satisfy the JAP to put in place a
policy covering this.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Climate, Environment, and Waste has decided to approve recommendations on restrictive covenants in parks.

decision_maker: Leader – Cabinet Member for Infrastructure and Corporate Strategy
purpose:
A petition entitled Stop Cancellation of
2026 Southend election was tabled at Council on 9 July 2025.
The petition calls on Southend-on-Sea City Council (the Council) to
provide assurances that it remains committed to holding the
scheduled local elections in May 2026 and will not seek a deferral
for these from central Government.
content:
A petition entitled Stop Cancellation of
2026 Southend election was tabled at Council on 9 July 2025.
The petition calls on Southend-on-Sea City Council (the Council) to
provide assurances that it remains committed to holding the
scheduled local elections in May 2026 and will not seek a deferral
for these from central Government.
 

That the petitioner be requested to note that
the Leader of the Council and Cabinet Member for Infrastructure and
Corporate Strategy provides reassurance to the petition organiser
through the publication of this decision record that no processes
to seek or secure the postponement of the May 2026 Local Elections
in Southend have been initiated by the Council.
 

The petition ‘Stop cancellation of 2026
Southend election’ ran from 3 March to 8 May 2025 and
received 183 signatures.
 
The petition calls on the
Council to provide assurances that it remains committed to holding
the scheduled local elections in May 2026 and will not seek a
deferral for these from central Government. It also references the
decision by Essex County Council to postpone its 2025 local
elections due to devolution arrangements and expresses concern that
Southend could face a similar outcome.
 
The concerns raised by
petitioners relate to the preservation of democratic rights and the
importance of maintaining regular electoral cycles.
 
The Council is elected
“by thirds” (i.e., one third of the councillors elected
at a time), with every fourth year being a “fallow”
year where local elections do not take place.
 
2025 was a fallow year for
Southend, and elections in thirds are planned for 2026 as per the
normal electoral cycle for Southend.
 
Any request to postpone
Southend’s elections for 2026 would require an order from the
Secretary of State before the year of any election could be
changed.
 
In July 2025, the Council voted
on the resolution to “not request any unnecessary delay,
postponement or cancellation” to elections in
2026.
 
On 18 December 2025, the
Minister of State for Local Government and Homelessness, Alison
McGovern MP, wrote to council leaders in local government
reorganisation areas with elections in May 2026. Her letter invited
councils to set out their views on the potential postponement of
their local election in May 2026 and whether doing this would allow
them to better deliver local government reorganisation.
Representations were requested to be submitted by 15 January
2026.
 
On 21 December 2025, the Leader
of the Council publicly confirmed that he would not be responding
to the invitation to request postponement outlined in 3.8 of this
report, and that 2026 elections would proceed as
scheduled.
 
At an Extraordinary meeting on
12 January 2026, the Council confirmed it wishes for the local
elections to proceed, as planned, and take place in May 2026 and
therefore not make any representations to Government for the
cancelation or postponement of elections.
 
The Leader of the Council has
taken into account the requests made in the petition and can
confirm that the Council remains committed to undertaking its local
election in 2026 as planned, in accordance with the statutory
timetable and electoral regulations.

As there is a precedent for postponing local
elections when devolution and local government reorganisation is in
progress, the Council could decide to make representation to
government asking it to consider postponing its 2026 local
elections.
 
This would have necessitated the formal
submission of a letter of representation to the Secretary of State
by midnight on 15 January 2026.
topline: The Leader of the Southend-on-Sea City Council has decided to proceed with the scheduled local elections in May 2026, rejecting calls for postponement.

content:
The sub-committee received a
report of the Executive Director (Environment & Place)
concerning an application by Hadi Yousefi for a Premises Licence at
Black & Red Turkish Supermarket, 153 High Street,
Southend-on-Sea, SS1 1LL.
 
The application sought to allow
the supply of alcohol for consumption off the premises from 09:00
to 23:00 hrs daily and the opening hours of the premises from 07:00
to 23:00 hrs daily.
 
The application was presented
by the applicant who gave evidence in support of the
application. 
 
The sub-committee noted that no
representations had been received from any of the Responsible
Authorities, although conditions had been agreed between the
applicant, Essex Police and the Environmental Protection Team
should the application be granted.
 
One (1) representation had,
however, been received from a local resident. A copy of their
written representations was provided to the sub-committee in
advance of the hearing. The objector also attended the hearing and
gave evidence.
 
Their objection related to the
four licensing objectives namely: the prevention of crime and
disorder, public safety, the prevention of public nuisance and the
protection of children from harm. 
 
The objector contested that the
measures proposed by the applicant to promote the licensing
objectives as outlined in the risk assessment were not preventive
and that granting the application would worsen existing issues of
crime, disorder and antisocial behaviour linked to street?drinking
citing incidents such as assault, indecent exposure, sexual
activity in public, prostitution, urination and defecation, drug
use and dealing, littering, begging, and loitering. These incidents
were based on evidence between 2018-2025 which included
observations and reporting of crime and disorder activity within
the area whilst noting that most crimes reported within the
postcode were not prosecuted. There were already a number of
premises in the vicinity already selling alcohol, three of which
were licensed to sell alcohol 24 hours a day. They contested that
the measures proposed by the applicant in the risk assessment to
address the issues of concern had been copied and pasted from the
measures proposed by the Police.
 
The objector also contested
that they believed the granting of this licence would further
compromise public safety and add to noise and disturbance already
affecting residents and visitors in the Milton Ward area. The
objector also raised concerns about the potential impact on
children who may be exposed to harmful behaviour and have their
safe participation in local events affected. Refusal of the
application would therefore help prevent crime in the first
instance and would promote child safety as well as the safe
attendance at local events on the High Street. They further
contested that the premises was located within a Public Space
Protection Order (PSPO) area, which would be considered an
unsuitable location for off-licence alcohol sales, and a
non-drinking zone.
 
The sub-committee carefully
considered all the evidence submitted in writing and orally at the
meeting. It listened to all the evidence and submissions and read
all the documents.  It had regard to the Statutory
Guidance Notes and Southend-on-Sea City Council’s Statement
of Licensing Policy. It considered the four licensing objectives
namely the prevention of crime and disorder, public safety, the
prevention of public nuisance and the protection of children from
harm. Each contested application is decided on its
merits.
 
The sub-committee was conscious
that the Responsible Authorities were all experts in their
respective fields (paragraph 9.12 of the Revised Guidance issued
under section 182 of the Licensing Act 2003 refers) and none had
raised any concerns in respect of the application. The applicant
had also agreed appropriate or amended conditions with Essex Police
and Environmental Health should the application be
granted.
 
The sub-committee was also
mindful that the number of licensed premises or the question of
whether another premises is needed are not matters for the
sub-committee to consider. Whilst the need for a specific business
or activity might be a relevant consideration for planning
permission or market forces, it is not a matter that the licensing
authority is primarily concerned with when assessing a licensing
application. There is no cumulative impact policy for this
area.
 
The sub-committee recognised
and appreciated the concerns expressed by the objector but
concurred with the applicant that there was no substantive evidence
as required under paragraph 9.43 of the revised guidance issued
under Licensing Act 2003 to substantiate  that the concerns of anti-social behaviour and
risks to public safety in the area would occur as a result of the
activities of off-licence premises. Drinking of alcohol in a PSPO
area was not a criminal offence and there is no legislation
prohibiting an off-licence from selling alcohol in the area.
Furthermore, should any issues arise from the licensed activities
at the premises, Section 51 of the Licensing Act 2003 provided a
statutory mechanism for initiating a Premises Licence Review to
address and manage such concerns.
 
The sub-committee concluded
that, based on the evidence presented to it in respect of this
application, there was insufficient evidence to substantiate that
the concerns raised in the representation would occur or could be
attributed to this premises or that could not be addressed through
the imposition of appropriate conditions. 
 
The sub-committee therefore,
did not consider that the promotion of the licensing objectives
would be undermined by the granting of the application, subject to
the imposition of appropriate conditions agreed with the
Responsible Authority.
 
Resolved:-
 
That the application for the
supply of alcohol for consumption off the premises from 09:00 hrs
to 23:00 hrs daily and the opening hours of the premises from 07:00
hrs to 23:00 hrs daily at Black & Red Turkish Supermarket,153
High Street, Southend-on-Sea, SS1 1LL be granted subject
to:
 
(1) The Mandatory Conditions
set out in Appendix 1 to the submitted report of the Executive
Director (Environment & Place); and
 
(2) The conditions submitted by
the applicant drawn from the operation schedule and the conditions
agreed between the applicant, the Essex Police and the
Environmental Protection Team as set out in Appendix 2 to the
submitted report of the Executive Director Environment &
Place).
topline: The sub-committee has decided to grant a Premises Licence for the supply of alcohol at Black & Red Turkish Supermarket in Southend-on-Sea, despite objections from a local resident.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities
purpose:
To seek delegated authority to the Executive
Director for Adults and Communities and Executive Director Children
& Public Health in consultation with the respective Portfolio
Holders:
1. To award the All-Age Carers Support services contract to the
successful tenderer from the 1st April 2026 for an initial period
of three years with an option to extend for a further period of two
years.
2. To issue extensions to this contract following its award. Such
authority includes finalising any negotiations and entering into
legal agreement for service provision from 1st April 2026 to 31st
March 2031 (if necessary) until a subsequent contract is
procured/awarded.
content:
The Cabinet Member
for (Social Care and Healthier Communities) agrees:
 
1.    
To award the All-Age Carers Support Service contract to the
successful provider identified in accordance with the outcome of
the procurement exercise, for an initial 3-year term (with option
to extend for 2 years) at a maximum total value of
£1,257,065.
2.    
To delegate the award of the contract (at 2.1 of the report) to
the Executive Director for Adult and Communities and Executive
Director for Children and Public Health to finalise and authorise
the entering into of all necessary documentation to facilitate the
award and /or extension of any contract. 
 

The proposed decision is driven the local
authority’s requirement to commission statutory support
services for all age carers under the following legislations.
 

·      
The Care Act 2014 specifically requires local authorities to assess
the needs of adult carers, identify their wellbeing needs, and
provide support where eligible. This includes offering information,
advice, and services to help carers maintain their own health and
wellbeing.

·      
Children Act 1989 and Children and Families Act 2014 ensure that
young carers (under 18) are identified, assessed, and provided with
the support they need, preventing them from undertaking
inappropriate levels of care that could impact their education,
health, or development.
 
A carer is anyone who looks after, gives help
or support, unpaid, to family members, friends, neighbours, or
others because of long-term physical or mental ill health,
disability, substance misuse, or challenges related to old age.
Carers are identified by the support they provide, not by whether
they live with the person they care for.
 
Carers play a crucial role in preventing the
need for formal, paid care and support for the individuals they
assist. This role is often highly demanding, both physically and
mentally. Despite the challenges, many carers do not view their
responsibilities as burdensome, but rather as a natural duty driven
by love and respect for their family members and friends. Carers
are not defined solely by their caregiving responsibilities; they
are, first and foremost, parents, siblings, relatives, and friends.
Caring is one of many roles they fulfil, rather than their primary
identity.
 
Carers First were awarded the contract for the
delivery of the Carers Support Service on 1st October 2021, and it
expires on 31st March 2026. This service providers a
single point of coordination for carers in Southend, providing
general and tailored information, advice, guidance, and support to
carers. The service also provides support carers to take ad hoc
appointment breaks from their caring role and to access necessary
appointments.
 
With the current Carers Support Service
contract ending, there is an opportunity to use information from
the Southend-on-Sea Carers Survey and wider research to commission
a new contract that better meets the diverse needs of carers in
Southend-on-Sea.
 
Carers First was originally commissioned to
provide support exclusively for adult carers. However, in June
2024, contract variation was implemented to include the provision
of support for young carers as part of a pilot initiative. This
amendment allows for the evaluation of the expanded service in
addressing the needs of both adult and young carers, with the pilot
set to run in line with the contract duration until 31st
March 2026.
 
Originally, the contract did not include
delivering statutory carers assessments. However, on the
1st June 2023, an additional contract variation to
include a pilot for undertaking these assessments was agreed.
 
This pilot was a success, and we have now
included this into the contract.
 
A review of the service, as well as
consultation with stakeholders and residents have informed the
development of the new all-age carers support service
specification.
 
The statutory duties to identify, assess, and
support unpaid carers are underpinned by key legislation, including
the Care Act 2014, which places duties on local authorities to
assess adult carers’ needs and provide appropriate
support.
 
For young carers, the Children Act 1989 and
the Children and Families Act 2014 require local authorities to
assess and meet their needs, ensuring their wellbeing, education,
and development are not negatively impacted by their caring
responsibilities.
 
These duties are further supported by guidance
such as Working Together to Safeguard Children 2023 and the
Children’s Social Care National Framework 2023, which promote
a whole-family, early intervention approach. Additionally, the
Equality Act 2010 and the Human Rights Act 1998 provide a broader
legal framework to ensure carers are not discriminated against or
disadvantaged due to their caring.
 
The recommendation for award of the All Age
Carers Support Service follows a comprehensive competitive
procurement process and rigorous evaluation to ensure high
standards and value for money.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Social Care and Healthier Communities has decided to award the All-Age Carers Support Service contract to a provider for an initial 3-year term.

decision_maker: Leader – Cabinet Member for Infrastructure and Corporate Strategy
purpose:
Approval is sought to appoint Balfour Beatty
contractor to deliver pre-construction services and early works for
the Leigh Port Redevelopment project. This will include key
deliverables such as procurement of major packages and site
compound requirements, temporary works design, site access
planning, development of the construction programme, health and
safety compliance, liaison with stakeholders and statutory bodies
as required and completion of essential surveys before
construction. These activities will ensure site readiness for main
construction starting in October 2026.
content:
1. The Leigh Port Regeneration
Project requires approval to commence pre?construction and early works to enable
main construction to commence in October 2026.
 
2. The project has moved
through design and value engineering and now needs the Principal
Contractor in place to lead programme development and to discharge
Principal Contractor duties under CDM 2015. This will include
taking responsibility for temporary works planning and associated
procurement, undertaking necessary surveys, as well as engaging
with the wider supply chain to secure accurate pricing for the main
construction works.

To appoint a new Principal
Contractor. This option was rejected to
maintain continuity and avoid abortive work. The current Principal
Contractor has already undertaken key activities, including
buildability reviews, initial supply chain engagement, construction
programming, and cost planning. They have also supported value
engineering, contributing to a reduction in overall project costs.
Appointing a new contractor at this stage would duplicate effort,
require revalidation of existing work, and introduce delays and
additional costs, making it inefficient and impractical within the
programme timeline and available budget.
topline: The Leader – Cabinet Member for Infrastructure and Corporate Strategy has decided to maintain the current Principal Contractor for the Leigh Port Regeneration Project to avoid duplication of effort and additional costs.

of the procurement process.

digital, data and ICT team, the wider workforce requires upskilling
to modernise service delivery across the board. Implementation of
Data and AI related apprenticeships are essential to delivering our
vision for a digitally confident, future-proof
workforce.
